newsitem.title: USA: US Labor's Reich wants more humane job cuts.
newsitem.headline: US Labor's Reich wants more humane job cuts.

text.p: U.S. Labor Secretary Robert Reich said Wednesday companies should take a longer-term, more humane approach to downsizing, the day after Sunbeam Corp announced it was halving its workforce.

"If you are trying to build a company that builds loyalty, expertise, skill and everything else, you've got to look five years out; you've got to take a much longer approach," Reich said on CNBC television.
Reich said it was unfortunate that firms viewed their workers as costs of production rather than assets, and treated their workforces "like disposable pieces of machinery."
"The stock price might go up in the short term, but in the long term if you do not have loyal and committed workers you are not going to show profits on the bottom line," Reich said.
Some companies had found ways to scale down in a more humane way, he said.
On Tuesday, Sunbeam said it was halving its workforce to 6,000 in a cost-cutting program meant to save $225 million.
Reich said he was commenting in general terms. "I don't comment on specific companies. It would be presumptious of me to second guess particular CEOs," he said.
